name: Vitreous paint (grisaille) fired on glass
process: The glass painter grinds a paint of finely powdered low-melting glass (a lead-silicate flux) and iron or copper oxide, mixes it with water or vinegar and gum arabic, and lays it on the cut pieces over the cartoon: first the trace lines, near-opaque, with a long brush; then washes (mattes) that are stippled, badgered or scratched out with a needle or stick to model light. Back-painting on the other face deepens the shading. The pieces are fired in a kiln at 650-700 degC so that the flux fuses the pigment to the glass, leaving a thin (10-100 um), uneven brown-black layer. Morris's firm drew with brown-black grisaille in this way from the cartoons, whose leads were marked in brown.
processSources: A. Rodrigues, M. L. Coutinho, C. Machado, L. Cerqueira Alves, A. Machado and M. Vilarigues, 'An Overview of Germanic Grisailles through the Stained-Glass Collection at Pena Palace', Heritage 5 (2022) 1003-1023, doi:10.3390/heritage5020055
A. Gilchrist, ''The tears wept by our windows': severe paint loss from stained glass windows of the mid-nineteenth century', Vidimus 64, https://www.vidimus.org/issue-64/feature-83/

composition.text: A mixture of finely ground glass, iron and/or copper oxide as pigment, applied with a vehicle (vinegar or water) and a temporary binder (gum arabic).
composition.source: A. Rodrigues, M. L. Coutinho, C. Machado, L. Cerqueira Alves, A. Machado and M. Vilarigues, 'An Overview of Germanic Grisailles through the Stained-Glass Collection at Pena Palace', Heritage 5 (2022) 1003-1023, doi:10.3390/heritage5020055

victorianRecipe.text: A mid-19th-century paint (Hardman) analysed: pigment about 50 % by weight, a hard lead-silicate flux (lead to silica about 3:2), coarsely ground iron-oxide particles.
victorianRecipe.source: A. Gilchrist, ''The tears wept by our windows': severe paint loss from stained glass windows of the mid-nineteenth century', Vidimus 64, https://www.vidimus.org/issue-64/feature-83/

photograph: Crisp, near-opaque dark trace lines; a granular, translucent brown haze of matting (thicker matte, less and browner light) with highlights scratched out; faint back-painting as a softer shadow.

unverified.reason: No measured transmittance of a fired grisaille matte per unit thickness was read.
